tasks.task: Get the brief and align with the project lead
tasks.what: Understand the client's expectations, scope and timeline.
tasks.how:
Get the brief from the project lead and check it against the standard scope (Scope & Context tab).
Hold a kick-off call with the project lead: scope, competitive set, markets, platforms, deliverable due date.
tasks.watch_out: Check whether Semantiweb ran this audit last year: it changes how every evolution is reported (see best practice).

tasks.what: Make sure your time on the project is planned.
tasks.how:
Check your staffing on Float.
Validate it with the project lead.

tasks.what: Get an accurate understanding of the brand ecosystem.
tasks.how:
Go to the brand website and identify the brand's official social media accounts.
Save the links in a dedicated section of your working sheet.
tasks.output: Brand accounts listed in the working sheet

tasks.task: Understand fashion vs beauty sales dynamics
tasks.what: Identify the key sales dynamics between fashion and beauty.
tasks.how:
Read articles and the annual report on the brand's fashion and beauty performance.
Understand the business dynamics: is it growing, where from, due to what?
Save the links in a dedicated section of your working sheet.
tasks.output: Sources and key dynamics in the working sheet

tasks.what: Get an accurate view of the brand's activations over the last 24 months in each market in scope: key fashion launches (fashion weeks, key events), beauty launches (fragrance, makeup, skincare) and their campaigns.
tasks.how:
Look at the brand's Instagram and TikTok accounts and at Google News.
Double-check with Claude for anything you may have missed.
List activations by type in your working sheet: date, type of event, link.
tasks.watch_out: Claude is a cross-check, not a source: keep a link for every activation.
tasks.output: Activation calendar in the working sheet

tasks.what: Check whether your competitive set was already covered by a recent audit, to reuse its volumes and adjust them at the margin.
tasks.how:
Ask your project lead and the analyst channels for the key decks, stating the competitive scope you are looking for.
Log the volumes and evolutions in your working sheet.
tasks.watch_out: Note the period each audit covers: a large time gap means re-running the competitor query (see 3.2).
tasks.output: Competitor volumes and evolutions in the working sheet

tasks.what: Crawl TikTok data (brand + competitors) with the Semantiweb crawlers.
tasks.how:
Identify 30 to 50 key brand and consumer hashtags (e.g. [brand hashtag], [brand hashtag], [brand hashtag]).
Corpus Manager ([internal link] > Sources / crawls > TikTok crawler ([internal link] > NEW PROJECT: one project for the brand, one for the competitors.
Check that the request appears in Slack #notif-corpus-manager-crawls and follow its progress.
tasks.watch_out: If the crawl is not finished after 2 working days, contact the Tech team on Slack.

tasks.what: Crawl Reddit data (brand + competitors) with the Semantiweb crawlers.
tasks.how:
Select the subreddits linked to the brand and its products, and to the competitors and their products.
Corpus Manager > Sources / crawls > Reddit crawler ([internal link] > NEW PROJECT: one project for the brand, one for the competitors.
Check that the request appears in Slack #notif-corpus-manager-crawls and follow its progress.
tasks.watch_out: If the crawl is not finished after 2 working days, contact the Tech team on Slack.

tasks.what: Collect the comments of the most commented TikTok videos with Export Comments.
tasks.how:
Check that the "Sorter For TikTok & Instagram" extension is installed on your computer.
On TikTok, search the brand / its products > Videos tab > sort by comments, descending > scroll down 10 times to refresh the data.
In your working sheet, list the 50 most commented videos: one column for the link, one for the number of comments.
In Export Comments, paste the video links and launch the export.
tasks.watch_out: If the crawl is not finished after 2 working days, contact the Tech team on Slack.

tasks.task: Collect e-commerce reviews (if R&R in scope)
tasks.what: Collect e-commerce reviews for the ratings & reviews analysis.
tasks.how:
List all key products of the brand and its competitors.
Check that they are in the Semantiweb reviews database: ICC > R&R - Semantiweb reviews Live Deduplicate.
If not, email the R&R crawl owner the products to crawl and the e-retailer scope (e.g. Sephora, as stated in the brief).
tasks.watch_out: If you are unsure about the e-retailer scope, validate it with the project lead. If the crawl is not finished after 2 working days, contact the Tech team on Slack.
tasks.output: Products available in the reviews database

tasks.what: Build the extraction query in Radarly or Meltwater.
tasks.how:
List the brand name and its variants, associated products, key events, celebrities and ambassadors, key hashtags (branded and organic).
In Radarly > New query, build it with the Claude skill "building radarly queries".
Reference: the [brand] example query

tasks.what: Get the volumes of the brands in the competitive set.
tasks.how:
Use the previous audits found in 1.4 and log volumes and evolutions in the working sheet.
If the time gap with that audit is significant, reuse the competitor query and create it in Radarly or Meltwater.
Adjust at the margin with the Radarly trend (Instagram only) over the months not covered.
tasks.output: Competitor volumes in the working sheet

tasks.task: Cross-check volumes in Talkwalker and Meltwater
tasks.what: In parallel, check volume, evolution and platform split in Talkwalker and Meltwater. These tools do not crawl, so volumes are available quickly.
tasks.how:
Talkwalker > Topic Analytics > select the brand > filters: Consumer voice + country + 2Y data > log volume and evolution by platform in the working sheet.
Meltwater: ask the Meltwater account owner on Slack for access > log volume and evolution by platform, especially TikTok.
tasks.watch_out: In Talkwalker, check that no other brands are pre-selected; deselect them if they are.
tasks.output: Talkwalker and Meltwater volumes by platform

tasks.what: If TikTok needs more volume than Meltwater gives, log the Spate and Visibrain volumes.
tasks.how:
Spate: Trends and/or Brands sections > enter branded hashtags (e.g. #[brand]: number of posts) > log the volumes in the working sheet.
Visibrain: get your own access and follow the Visibrain guide to build a query.
tasks.watch_out: Ask your project lead for the Spate access. Never copy logins into shared documents.
tasks.output: Spate / Visibrain volumes in the working sheet

tasks.what: Send the project lead a recommendation for the final volume.
tasks.how:
One recommendation per platform: Instagram normally from Radarly or Meltwater, Reddit from Radarly or Meltwater, TikTok from Meltwater.
Fact-check the evolutions with Talkwalker.
tasks.watch_out: A large volume gap between tools can signal a query issue: are we missing a viral topic?
tasks.output: Final volume validated by the project lead

tasks.what: Build the brand corpus in Corpus Manager.
tasks.how:
Once the project lead has validated the query, run the Radarly / Meltwater extracts and load them into Corpus Manager.
Load the Meltwater TikTok extracts.
Load the TikTok hashtag crawls, Reddit crawls and Export Comments data.
Request or run the deduplication.
Reuse the standard facets and adapt them to the brand (rename products, campaigns, events; work with Claude). Ask for the [brand] or [brand] corpus facets in Slack #analysts.
tasks.watch_out: If ratings & reviews are in scope, build a separate reviews corpus (different facets and displays).
tasks.tools: Radarly, Meltwater, Corpus Manager, Export Comments, Claude, Slack
tasks.output: Deduplicated brand corpus with adapted facets

tasks.what: Build the competitor corpus in Corpus Manager.
tasks.how: Follow exactly the same steps as for the brand corpus (4.1).

tasks.what: As soon as the corpus is ready, run frequencies at country level for megabrand, fashion and beauty, on L12M and P12M.
tasks.how:
In your corpus, select the facets (country, timeline, fashion, etc.).
Run the frequencies in "Lexical & Hashtags".

tasks.what: Show the brand's key moments in beauty and fashion over the period.
tasks.how:
Explain each conversation peak.
Identify every peak and illustrate it with a visual (viral posts).
tasks.watch_out: Rule: if Semantiweb ran this audit last year, report evolutions against last year's audit, not against the current corpus.

tasks.what: Complete the conversation volume slides (megabrand, fashion, beauty).
tasks.how:
Give volumes and evolution.
Explain the dynamics: where it comes from, why, which platform.
tasks.watch_out: Rule: if Semantiweb ran this audit last year, report evolutions against last year's audit, not against the current corpus.

tasks.what: Add the competitive set (5 competitors max) to the volume slides.
tasks.how:
Reuse the data from the working sheet.
Explain the dynamics: where it comes from, why, which platform.
tasks.watch_out: Rule: if Semantiweb ran this audit last year, report evolutions against last year's audit, not against the current corpus.

tasks.what: Identify the top brands consumers associate with the audited brand (megabrand, fashion, beauty).
tasks.how:
From the corpus, pull the top frequencies on L24M and L12M.
Identify the top brands and those rising fastest.
tasks.watch_out: Rule: if Semantiweb ran this audit last year, report evolutions against last year's audit, not against the current corpus.

tasks.what: Show consumer sentiment and what drives it.
tasks.how:
Give the share of negative, neutral and positive sentiment.
Add the consolidated sentiment benchmark for each competitor.
Identify the drivers of positive and negative sentiment with visuals and top words (pull frequencies and read the verbatims).
tasks.watch_out: Rule: if Semantiweb ran this audit last year, report evolutions against last year's audit, not against the current corpus.

tasks.what: Build the brand equity analysis (image and uniqueness).
tasks.how: a/ Corpus frequencies (megabrand, beauty, fashion): pull frequencies on L24M and on L12M vs P12M (L12M over-index) to identify top words and top rising words.; b/ TikTok desk research (megabrand, beauty, fashion): mainly edit posts (aesthetics, fanbase). Identify key visuals and recurring keywords in comments. Collect about 30 key verbatims (usually fan comments).; c/ Values in the corpus (megabrand, beauty, fashion): look at the L12M vs P12M evolution of key values and log them in the working sheet. Which values matter most in brand equity? Which grow fastest? Where do fashion and beauty connect or disconnect (perceptions, aesthetics, brand universes)?
tasks.output: Image perception inputs in the working sheet

tasks.what: Validate the image perception before building slides.
tasks.how:
Send your image perception recommendation to the project lead.
Schedule a session to present your inputs.

tasks.what: Build brand equity perception slides
tasks.how:
Word clouds on https://wordart.com/ with the Playfair Display font, following the megabrand / fashion / beauty colour code.
Moodboards to illustrate the equity.
Fashion and beauty focus (word clouds).

tasks.what: Define the brand's uniqueness (USP) vs its competitors.
tasks.how: First ask whether the competitors were covered in a previous audit, and reuse that work as is (visuals and consumer semantic analysis).

tasks.what: Which topics are evolving? Are there new top topics?
tasks.how:
Use the corpus facets and read the verbatims.
Compare with last year's brand audit.

tasks.task: Fashion: deep dive on emblematic features
tasks.what: Which emblematic features are evolving? Are there new ones? What drives them (show, ambassadors, celebrity posts, TikTok trend)?
tasks.how:
Use the corpus facets and desk research.
Compare with last year's brand audit.

tasks.task: Fashion: deep dive on the creative director
tasks.what: What does the conversation around the creative director add to brand equity?
tasks.how:
Conversation volume and evolution.
Sentiment.
Visual moodboard.
Word cloud of top words and rising words.

tasks.what: (1) How does the product perform? (2) What does the launch add to brand equity?
tasks.how:
Ratings & reviews with a category benchmark: number of reviews, average rating, sampling rate, key attributes.
Social listening: volume, evolution, top words.

tasks.what: Indicate the audience's socio-demographic profile and centers of interest.
tasks.how: In HypeAuditor, generate the audience analysis of the brand accounts (beauty, fashion, all).
tasks.watch_out: Rule: if Semantiweb ran this audit last year, report evolutions against last year's audit, not against the current corpus.

tasks.task: Build consumer tribe ID cards (if requested)
tasks.what: Profile specific communities when the client wants a deep dive.
tasks.how: Build the tribes qualitatively: moodboard, top words, top products / brands associated, key usages and behaviors, key mindset, age and gender index.

tasks.what: Keep the project team aligned throughout the audit.
tasks.how: Plan at least 2 to 3 review calls per week with the project team.

tasks.what: Anticipate the restitution.
tasks.how:
Confirm with the project lead whether you should attend.
Make sure you have the invitation.

tasks.what: Get feedback on your work.
tasks.how: After the restitution, ask the project lead for written feedback (plus a quick coffee or call if needed).

deck.title: Brand Audit | Deck Structure
deck.description: Standard slide sequence of a brand audit deck, with the data each slide needs and when it is included.
rows: Megabrand perimeter (brand + sub-brands / franchises), period (L12M vs L12M-1), competitors, countries.
Section list with one visual per section.
Numbered learnings across sections: headline + evidence.
Same format as global key learnings, market-specific findings only.
Volume of conversations L12M-1 vs L12M per market, evolution %, brand vs competitors.
Beauty vs Fashion (or other categories) share of megabrand conversation per market, with evolution.
Share of voice vs competitors (megabrand, then x each category)
SoV per market with evolution; brand gap vs competitors, zoom on lagging sub-category.
Top brands associated (megabrand, then x each category)
% of brand posts mentioning another brand per market; top 10 with evolution vs PP; new entries / no longer in top 10.
Role of brand vs associated brand group (e.g. luxury vs indie) in routines; hashtags, top words, verbatims.
Competitor association mirrors (x each competitor, megabrand + category)
Top 10 brands associated with each competitor per market; brand rank in competitor's set.
USP statement; contribution of each category to the USP; what changed vs last audit.
Always (what's new if previous audit exists)
Megabrand perception vs competitors (x each market)
'Brand is X' headline per brand, 3 attributes each, visual, top words, verbatim.
Words specific to each brand, shared words across brands, one verbatim per brand.
Category perception vs competitors (x each category x each market)
Same as megabrand perception at category level (beauty, makeup, fragrance, skincare, fashion); hero products cited.
Specific vs shared codes (x each category)
Same as megabrand codes slide at category level.
Share of territories base 100 per brand with country split and evolution; shared territories.
Top territories split by category; emotional needs per market; local readings (e.g. territory expressed by product).
If overindexing territory or if requested
Activation types ranked (new products, gifting, pop-ups / IRL, sales) per brand per market, %, verbatim per type.
Mentions over the year, peaks annotated (seasonal occasions, local festivals, events), brand vs competitors.
Muse cards with share and evolution; perception words, overindexing words vs previous audit.
Share of volume, angle per market, verbatims. Flag low signal.
Top 3 success drivers with examples, visuals, verbatims.
Top 3 friction points turning engagement into frustration.
Strategy summary per brand; top mentions within pop-up conversations.
Brand vs competitors on activation criteria per market; what consumers expect now.
4 personas per slide: name, visual, brand affinity, growth flag, driver, 'they love'.
Topics ranked by volume per category, evolution L12M, all markets combined.
Same per market, with market-specific readings.
Category split of beauty conversation per market (base 100); top 3 to 4 products per category with evolution.
Desirability formula of the category in one statement + supporting paragraph.
Top 4 drivers ranked, market flags, visual and verbatim per driver.
Product desirability vs edge (x each category)
Products by family: rating, review volume, edge %; highest desirability and edge drivers flagged.
Emerging look or usage: hashtags, visuals, verbatims.
Hero vs new launches: evolution, claims, positioning shift.
Historic equity vs emerging expression; updated desirability formula; verbatims.
Category-level reuse of P1 / P2 / P4 slides
Associations, codes, perception per market, personas filtered on the category.
Awareness and review volume, perception, most reviewed products, SoV vs competitor lines, associations, codes, usage behaviours, personas.
Reviews corpus, franchise corpus, top brands, persona facets
Consumer mindset, drivers and topics ranked vs competitors, hero product perception, range expansion, associated brands, local nicknames.
Category corpus (one market), reviews, top brands
If category relevant in one market only
Audience overlap between categories / franchises (consumer POV, not co-mention only); contribution of each category to the megabrand.

Note: derived from the [brand] Beauty Brand Audit 2026 deck. 'Included when' conditions are inferred and to be validated by the project lead. P7 is a placeholder in the source deck (no slide built yet).
